jobs.description_text: SR. CHEMICAL ENGINEER, PCB (STARLINK/STARMIND) Starlink believes in providing fast, reliable internet to those that need it most. We design, build, and launch the world's largest and most advanced satellite constellation that is capable of delivering high-speed internet to even the most remote locations. As a Chemical Engineer on Starlink, you will spearhead state of the art production processes for our printed circuit boards (PCBs). You will design and implement environmentally friendly chemical recycling strategies, develop highly capable processes for use in mass production, and become a multi-disciplinary expert in PCB fabrication. Your work will form the backbone for millions of next generation consumer facing devices that we ship directly to customers and businesses all over the world. From private homes, RVs, planes, or boats, this team plays an instrumental role in leveling the playing field for high-speed connectivity. You will own various PCB production processes, from initial machine design to running hands-on process DOEs, and will interact regularly with senior leadership during critical design phases. jobs.title: Sr. CVD Equipment Engineer, Solar Cells (Starlink)
jobs.description_text: SR. CVD EQUIPMENT ENGINEER, SOLAR CELLS (STARLINK) Starlink believes in providing fast, reliable internet to those that need it most. We design, build, and launch the world's largest and most advanced satellite constellation that is capable of delivering high-speed internet to even the most remote locations. As a Sr. CVD Equipment Engineer for our solar cell factory, you will own the PECVD equipment used to manufacture silicon heterojunction solar cells at massive scale. You will work closely with our existing CVD Process Engineering team to ensure world-class equipment performance, reliability, and uptime. While the process team focuses on film properties and cell efficiency, you will be the hardware owner responsible for tool availability, stability, and scaling to support our ambitious goals. Your work will form the backbone of the Starlink network (photons of sunlight in is directly proportional to photons of data out to customers!) and help provide internet to tens of millions of customers all around the world. You will spearhead state of the art production equipment for an internal solar cell production line, providing high efficiency and high-quality solar cells for both our latest generation Starlink satellites and for Starship missions to the Moon and Mars. jobs.title: Sr. Cybersecurity Engineer (Starshield)
jobs.description_text: SR. CYBERSECURITY ENGINEER (STARSHIELD) At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy the Starshield constellation. Starshield is the world’s largest US government satellite constellation and is tasked with providing immediate access to critical intelligence and national security data for the US government anywhere on the globe. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – in-space sensors, on-the-ground receivers, data processing, and the mesh network that provides lightning-fast connectivity to users around the world. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starshield's global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help us further our ambitious goals. We are looking for a senior engineer to develop and continually test the cyber defenses of the Starshield network. This job will be hands-on and require breadth of experience in both software and security. A great candidate for this role appreciates a challenge, thrives on curiosity, and wants to make a difference in the world. RESPONSIBILITIES: This team's priority is to be prepared for immediate response to any active threat against our systems. Implement Starshield's cyber defense strategy. Continually assess the landscape of cyber threats and develop specific countermeasures for the Starshield systems. We are seeking an exceptional Sr. Device Physics Engineer to lead end-to-end cell efficiency ownership in our high-volume silicon heterojunction (SHJ) solar cell fab. Acting as the central process integration expert, you will collaborate with specialized process and equipment engineers to maximize cell performance to achieve state of the art efficiency, define wafer specifications, design space-optimized cell architectures, and establish comprehensive metrology and reliability frameworks. Your work will span from ingot growth all the way through cell production (wafer prep, deposition, passivation, metallization) and module fabrication. Your work will ensure our solar cells deliver unmatched power density and durability for Starship, Starlink, AI Satellites, and deep-space missions. As an electrical development engineer on the Starshield team, you will demonstrate extreme ownership through detailed and thorough design, hardware bring- up/characterization/testing, and requirements generation/verification - ultimately seeing your hardware through all aspects of its life cycle. Starshield is a quickly growing program with a wide range of engaging opportunities from blank-sheet design to on-orbit troubleshooting. You will work with many cross-disciplinary teams and will need to think at a system level to ensure that your design is viable. Our development timelines are quick and you will need to rigorously explore solutions for previously unsolved or unknown problems. Every day we push the limits of what is possible through innovation, determination, and teamwork to drive the mission to success. Realizing this vision demands highly reliable, high performance electrical hardware ranging from power electronics, high speed digital systems, mixed signal designs, robust avionics, networking, and custom compute electronics. These systems must operate in the extreme environment of space while delivering the connectivity, control, power distribution, and processing needed for orbital AI inference. The Starmind team designs, builds, and operates the orbital compute fabric of the future. We develop nearly every key piece of technology in house – from the satellites’ flight computers and power systems to the fully custom compute electronics, memory, and networking that form the brain of our on-orbit data centers. As a Senior Electrical Design Engineer on the Starmind Payload Engineering team, you’ll have ownership over the entire life-cycle of the hardware that enables advanced on-orbit AI processing and data center workloads. jobs.title: Sr. Fluids Systems Engineer, Production (Starship)
jobs.description_text: SR. FLUIDS ENGINEER, PRODUCTION (STARSHIP) Starship is the largest and most capable space launch system ever developed. With the capability to deliver in excess of 100 metric tons to Earth’s orbit, it will fundamentally change access to space, and is the technology that will be used to establish a self-sustaining city on Mars. We will ultimately need thousands of Starships to accomplish that feat. The Starbase production fluids team builds, maintains, and operates the fluid systems the Starship factory runs on. This includes high pressure production test equipment used to validate vehicles and components, vehicle press systems, and cleaning and contamination control equipment. Engineers on this team own hardware from problem statement through design, build, commissioning, and handoff to the technicians and operators who use it every day. We are looking for hands-on engineers who can reduce a messy production problem to first principles, design the simplest system that meets the requirement, and stay with it until it is fully handed off and documented. You will work directly with our build shop, partner teams, and production customers on an accelerated schedule. RESPONSIBILITIES: Design, build, and commission fluid systems for Starship production, including test systems, manufacturing systems, and cleaning equipment. jobs.description_text: SR. FULL STACK SOFTWARE ENGINEER (STARLINK) At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe. As a Sr. Full Stack Engineer, you will work closely with a mix of both external customers and internal partners across all engineering disciplines here at SpaceX to bring observability to a rapidly expanding network of millions of assets. The tools and applications you build will empower Starlink customers to manage their deployed assets in aviation, maritime, and enterprise environments while also bringing enhanced development to key features across various internal and external platforms. On this team, we will rely on you to be a key figure in the successful development of mission critical, high performance web applications. MANUFACTURING ENGINEER, SOLAR CELL FACTORY (STARLINK) At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system — thousands of satellites, ground station gateways, and consumer antennae that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing. These cells have to be high-performance, low-cost, and ultra-reliable, and the factory that builds them has to ramp quickly without giving up yield. As a manufacturing engineer for solar cells, you will own the production processes and equipment that turn development hardware into full-rate manufacturing. You will drive the line from early process concept through commissioning, qualification, and sustained production, and you will be the link between engineering development and the factory floor. jobs.title: Structural Engineer, Starship Tower
jobs.description_text: STRUCTURAL ENGINEER, STARSHIP TOWER The Starship catch tower will redefine ground support systems for launch vehicles as we know them, with the ultimate goal of launching, catching, and relaunching orbital boosters in hours or days instead of weeks or months. The tower the largest steel structure ever built to support a launch vehicle. It must survive the acoustic, thermal, and blast environment of the most powerful rocket in the world at liftoff, absorb the loads of catching a returning booster, and then be ready to do it again within days. As the Structural Engineer on the Tower team, you will own the structural integrity of these structures from concept through fabrication, erection, activation, and launch operations. You will perform and own the structural design and analysis of primary and secondary steel, connections, anchorage, and foundation interfaces; develop and issue drawings, calculations, and specifications; and lead consulting engineers, fabricators, and construction contractors through engineering, procurement, fabrication, construction, and commissioning. You will work hand in hand with the mechanical, mechanisms, fluids, and analysis engineers on the team to ensure the structure meets requirements for both the design and the manufacturing and integration processes. Starshield's proliferated low-Earth orbit architecture provides inherent resiliency and constant connectivity to on-orbit assets, while SpaceX's proven rapid launch capability provides expedient and economical access to space. This includes designing tooling (electrical checkout racks, vehicle harnessing, DAQ setups, etc.) and processes (vehicle checkout software, harness/component integration, troubleshooting procedures, etc.) to build Starshield vehicles at a continually increasing and rapid cadence. You’ll become an expert in the challenges facing modern legal departments—from fragmented intake and manual workflows to AI adoption, contract processes, and cross-functional collaboration—and translate those challenges into compelling product stories and go-to-market programs. jobs.title: Senior Staff Electrical Engineer - Payload
jobs.description_text: We are seeking a highly skilled Senior Staff ElectricalEngineer to lead the design, development, integration, test, and flight qualification of advanced spaceborne payloads. This post focuses on the role of Payload Lead Engineer (aka Responsible Engineer) in our Phased Array product line, focusing on Ka-band Active Electronically Steered Arrays (AESAs). CesiumAstro AESAs are state-of-the-art electronics assemblies consisting of an antenna element array, RF electronics, digital array control, and power conversion – engineered into a single box using a modular but optimized approach. The Payload Lead is responsible for the technical development of a new payload product consisting of a phased array (AESA) and a processing unit (RPU). This combines deep, multi-disciplinary technical accountability with responsibility for on-time schedule execution. The Payload Lead is the leader of the multidisciplinary technical team, the primary point of contact for the program manager, and often a key interface point for our customers. Success in this role requires deep expertise in technical topics as well as project management, leadership, and communication in a fast-paced startup environment.

jobs.title: Research Scientist Intern, AI Molecular Design (Winter/Spring)
jobs.description_text: GenBio AI is an AI for Science company on a mission to make biology fully computable. We are building AIDO (AI-Driven Digital Organism) to simulate living systems, decode biology holistically, and accelerate medical and scientific research. Our first step toward that mission is AIDO Cell, the first virtual cell world model that holistically simulates cell biology from molecules up to whole-cell behavior. It enables researchers to run experiments virtually, predicting how cells respond to genetic changes, drugs and other interventions before going into the lab. It is supported by AIDO Foundry, an AI-builds-AI engineering framework for automating virtual cell development, and AIDO Lab, an interface to digitally run experiments and observe the results. Together they form the foundation for a new paradigm in AI-driven drug discovery, bioengineering, and fundamental biomedical research.

jobs.title: 3D Computer Vision Researcher – Remote (US)
jobs.location_raw: Remote, USA: AL, AZ, CO, DC, FL, GA, IL, IN, MA, MD, ME, MN, NC, NJ, NM, NY, OH, OR, PA, TN, TX, UT, VA, WI
jobs.description_text: Advance 3D Vision Research from Algorithms to Open Source Applications. In this position, you’ll research and develop algorithms for photogrammetry, camera calibration, registration, and 3D reconstruction from images and video. Current projects emphasize aerial and satellite imagery, with opportunities to adapt these capabilities to new challenges and data domains such as underwater imagery and synthetic aperture radar. Your work will contribute to open source applications and frameworks including TeleSculptor, KWIVER, and Danesfield. You’ll also explore how 3D vision can support broader computer vision problems such as object detection and tracking, change detection, super resolution, and video compression. Kitware partners with government R&D agencies, branches of the U.S. military, members of the Intelligence Community, and commercial organizations ranging from startups to Fortune 500 companies. You’ll have opportunities to collaborate directly with customers, participate in field tests and demonstrations, publish novel work, and apply state-of-the-art artificial intelligence approaches to real-world national security challenges.

During environmental campaigns, you will work alongside the engineer responsible for mechanical testing, providing electrical test support and functional verification. On-site in Arlington, Texas. You will work in an environment with competing asks, real ambiguity, and high expectations, and you will need to make calls about what gets done, in what order, and what does not, without waiting for permission. This role is internally facing. E-Space is in Stealth Mode while we build our technology, so the role does not include external communications or PR. This is a hands-on role: approximately 60% of your time will involve drafting applications, with approximately 30–40% devoted to prosecution. You will personally draft most assigned applications and all U.S. Office Action responses for assigned matters, and review outside counsel’s non-U.S. Office Action responses. The role calls for an experienced practitioner who can produce high-quality work with limited supervision and is proficient using AI-based tools effectively.

The target base pay for this position is $160,000 - $195,000 annually. The total compensation packaged will be determined by various factors such as your relevant job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. jobs.title: Backend Software Engineer - Data Connectors
jobs.description_text: The Role The Connectivity team builds the software that connects Palantir’s platform to customer systems. Our connectors integrate databases, enterprise applications, cloud storage, web services, and streaming systems, enabling customers to bring data into Foundry and write back to their operational systems. From large datasets to real-time events and user-driven interactions, these connections underpin the applications and AI workflows customers build with Foundry and AIP. You’ll build and maintain Foundry’s first-class connector suite and the shared infrastructure behind it. You’ll work across the stack, taking ownership of connector implementations, developer SDKs, and the systems that build, test, distribute, and run our connectivity software. A central part of this work is evolving and scaling a large, established codebase. You’ll move integrations from bespoke infrastructure onto shared platform capabilities, design SDKs that enable other teams and customers to build integrations independently, and safely retire older implementations. You’ll also build observability and diagnostic tools that help users understand, monitor, and troubleshoot their connections. You’ll own improvements from design through production and use what you learn from operating connectors to strengthen the platform they share.

You’ll help build Foundry’s first-class connector suite and the shared infrastructure behind it. You’ll work across the stack, taking ownership of connector implementations, developer SDKs, and the systems that build, test, distribute, and run our connectivity software. Working alongside experienced engineers, you will take on real problems in our production systems. That could mean adding a capability to a Connector, contributing to the infrastructure that runs our assets, or building features to ensure the performance, reliability, and observability of our connectivity suite. jobs.title: GNC Engineer - Controls
jobs.description_text: About the Role The GNC team at Pivotal develops the flight control and navigation algorithms that let our aircraft fly safely and precisely, including on the Helix family of aircraft. We are looking for a GNC Engineer II who focuses on flight controls to evaluate and tune our existing control laws, so the aircraft has stable, responsive, and predictable handling across the flight envelope. You will use CONDUIT and our existing simulation environment to analyze the control laws against stability and performance criteria, tune their gains, and check their behavior in Monte Carlo and full-mission simulations before they go to flight test. You will work closely with the GNC engineers who own the control law architecture, as well as the firmware, aeromechanical, and flight test teams. The ideal candidate has a solid grounding in linear control theory and aircraft flight dynamics, and enjoys the analytical work of understanding why a control system behaves the way it does and how to improve it. Experience with frequency-domain control system analysis is highly desirable.

jobs.title: GNC Engineer - Navigation
jobs.description_text: About the Role The GNC team at Pivotal develops the flight control and navigation algorithms that let our aircraft fly safely and precisely, including on the Helix family of aircraft. We are looking for a GNC Engineer II who focuses on navigation to design, implement, and verify the state estimation and sensor fusion algorithms. These algorithms estimate the aircraft’s attitude, heading, position, velocity, and other critical states in real time. You will work across the full development lifecycle. That includes characterizing sensors and designing algorithms in MATLAB and Simulink, deploying them on embedded flight hardware, testing them in simulation and hardware-in-the-loop, and analyzing flight test data. You will work closely with the flight controls, firmware, avionics, autonomy, systems engineering, and flight test teams. The ideal candidate has a solid grounding in estimation theory and hands-on experience taking a filter from design all the way to real sensor data or hardware. Experience with aircraft navigation systems, GNSS/INS integration, and eVTOL or UAV platforms is highly desirable.

The ideal candidate is a fully qualified flight controls engineer who works independently, has designed and tuned control laws that were evaluated in flight test or piloted simulation, ideally on VTOL, rotorcraft, or eVTOL aircraft, and brings sound judgment to interpreting analysis and test results.

jobs.title: Staff GNC Engineer – Flight Controls
jobs.description_text: About the Role The GNC team at Pivotal develops the flight control and navigation algorithms that let our aircraft fly safely and precisely, including on the Helix family of aircraft. We are looking for a Staff GNC Engineer to lead flight control law development on an aircraft program: owning the control law architecture and its design, tuning, and verification from simulation through flight test. You will also be a team lead for flight controls, setting priorities for the team, overseeing its technical work, and mentoring the engineers on it, while working closely with the navigation, firmware, aeromechanical, systems engineering, safety, and flight test teams. The ideal candidate has a track record of taking flight control laws from design to flight on real aircraft, ideally VTOL, rotorcraft, or eVTOL, and the judgment to make sound design and flight test decisions with incomplete information. This role is a strong next step for an engineer who has grown through hands-on flight controls work and is ready to lead a team.

Your primary objective will be to optimize and modernize our loan verification process, moving from manual, touch-heavy procedures to a streamlined, automated operational workflow. In this role, you will lead, mentor, and motivate our Loan Operations teams in Phoenix and San Francisco, while also overseeing our vendor partnerships. You will champion a strategic approach to scaling our business—focusing on scaling through workflow efficiencies and process improvements rather than linear staffing growth. Reporting to the Director of Operations, you will manage operational processes, oversee key vendor relationships, and identify opportunities to integrate modern solutions to improve department-wide productivity & quality. Compensation details: The salary for this position is $87,000 - $105,000 annually, plus bonus and generous benefits.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Operational Procurement
jobs.description_text: General Summary The Associate Director of Operational Procurement leads key operational procurement activities that ensure material availability, supply continuity, and efficient business operations. This role requires experience in procurement operations, raw material planning, systems and process knowledge, and team leadership experience. This leader will partner closely with Ops Leadership in Supply Chain, Strategic Procurement, and Logistics, as well as leadership in our Accounts Payable and IT teams to drive continuous process improvements across the procurement organization. A successful candidate will bring hands-on expertise managing direct and indirect procurement processes and systems, including purchasing, material planning, inventory optimization, shortage mitigation, and supplier enablement. Experience working with SAP, Coupa, MRP, and procure-to-pay systems is highly desired. jobs.title: Associate Principal Supplier Quality Engineer – Supplier Development
jobs.description_text: General Summary We are establishing a dedicated Supplier Development capability within Supplier Quality Engineering focused on strategic supply chain initiatives, strengthening supplier capability, and improving long-term supply continuity and resiliency. The Associate Principal Supplier Quality Engineer (Supplier Development) will serve as a technical and program leader for high-priority supplier initiatives, partnering with Strategic Procurement and cross-functional stakeholders to define strategy, align resources, manage interdependent workstreams, and drive programs through execution. This is an opportunity to help shape and grow an emerging organization while leading initiatives with broad business visibility, cross-functional influence, and long-term impact. This position is responsible for leading complex, cross-functional supplier development programs spanning supplier qualification, capability improvement, risk reduction, and supply continuity. The role will establish program plans, integrate technical and business requirements, manage risks and dependencies, and mobilize internal and external stakeholders to improve supplier quality, scalability, process robustness, and readiness to support business growth. The individual will provide technical leadership across a portfolio of supplier initiatives and influence decisions that affect supply continuity, product quality, and long-term supplier strategy. jobs.title: Calibration and Equipment Systems Engineer I
jobs.description_text: General Summary The Calibration and Equipment Systems Engineer I serves as a subject matter expert (SME) in calibration and metrology within the Equipment Maintenance department. This position plays a critical role in maintaining the integrity of measurement systems used across Production, Quality, and R&D. The engineer leads out-of-tolerance (OOT) investigations, supports equipment qualifications and change controls, and provides technical guidance to calibration staff. In addition, supports the development and maintenance of equipment asset management software tools and databases, and interfaces with IT to ensure data integrity and system reliability. Ensures alignment with internal Quality Management System (QMS) procedures and applicable regulatory standards, contributing to audit readiness, continuous improvement, and equipment compliance across the organization. jobs.title: IT Experience Services Specialist II
jobs.description_text: The IT Experience Services Specialist II serves as an advanced technical resource within the IT Experience Services team, providing high-quality end-user support and ensuring a white glove service experience across all communication channels, including Talkdesk & Microsoft Teams phone support, Microsoft Teams chat, and ServiceNow incident and request management. This role independently resolves complex issues, manages escalations, and handles out-of-scope or non-standard requests that require advanced troubleshooting, coordination, and technical judgment. The IT Experience Services Specialist II supports employees with IT issues involving PC, Mac, and mobile devices; local and SaaS applications; and network and enterprise IT services. In addition to supporting corporate offices, this role provides on-site and remote technical assistance for manufacturing facilities, ensuring minimal disruption to production operations and adherence to IT and security standards in regulated environments. Key responsibilities include diagnosing and resolving advanced technical incidents, coordinating hardware deployment and configuration, performing hardware repairs, documenting, and managing escalations in ServiceNow, identifying systemic issues and trends, and recommending process improvements. The role also participates in cross-functional IT projects, supports manufacturing IT operations, and provides mentorship and guidance to Tier I support staff.
